body.statement: For every component-respecting \(h\)-net, \(e_h\le\bar e_h=(K+L)h+Gh^\beta\). The extrema of the finite outer linear objective \(J_{P,h}^{\mathrm{out}}\) over \(\mathcal U_h^{\mathrm{out}}\) are attained and differ from \(V_P^-\) and \(V_P^+\) by at most \(\bar e_h+Lh\), using \(\|\nu_P\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1\). Every value of \(J_{P,h}^{\mathrm{in}}\) is attained by a member of \(\mathcal C_P\), and the inner objective range is within \(2Lh\) of the full objective range. Consequently the induced inner and outer WAOSS intervals have Hausdorff error at most \(A^{-1}(\bar e_h+2Lh)\). These conclusions hold when rectangle boundaries touch, when a connected component is separated from \(z=0\), and when obstacle constraints bind.
body.justification: The theorem makes the sharp continuous-support set computable with a certified deterministic error.
body.gap: Freyberger and Horowitz (2015) start with finite discrete support, while Voronin (2025) analyzes values of programs already finite.
body.consumer: A software implementation can report sharp WAOSS bounds together with a mesh certificate rather than an undocumented gridding tolerance.
